Routes

Six routes cross the town centre, and four of them share the same stop outside the public library.

Acme Transit runs the eastern loop on a twenty minute headway from six in the morning until half past eleven at night. Northwind Traders sponsors the two school services, which is why those two carry a different livery from the rest of the fleet. The western loop is the only one that leaves the valley, and it is also the only one that keeps a timetable on paper.

A rider who changes at the library pays once, as long as the second bus is boarded inside ninety minutes. Nobody advertises this, and the drivers are used to explaining it. See the stop table for the figures behind it.

Stops

Stops are numbered from the depot outward, which means the numbering runs backwards along the western loop. It has been that way since the loop was reversed in the spring, and renumbering a hundred and forty signs has never reached the top of anyone's list.

Shelters

Forty one stops have a shelter. Eleven of those have a timetable case, and six of the cases have a timetable in them. The rest were emptied when the printed timetable was retired and never refilled.

Lighting

Lighting is the complaint that arrives most often, and it is the one the town can act on without asking anyone's permission, so it is usually fixed inside a fortnight.

Fares

A single is a flat fare. A day pass pays for itself on the third boarding, which is the number most riders reach on a weekday without planning to. Jane Doe, who has driven the eastern loop for eleven years, says the only fare question she is ever asked is whether the pass works on the school services. It does.

Further reading: the rider survey, the network handbook, and the patronage log.

Footnotes

Figures are invented. Names are the usual placeholders: Acme Corp, Northwind Traders, Jane Doe, John Smith. Any resemblance to a real bus network is a coincidence and probably a coincidence worth looking into.
